scripts.build.rust_tool_env.prepare_shar.decoded_text:
Start the shared compiler cache before entering a command's job.

    Never restart an existing server: other lanes may still be using it. A
    reachable server needs no `--start-server` spawn. A failed or timed-out
    start raises unless a concurrent start made the server reachable meanwhile.
    Callers then disable the wrapper for that one command (the Rust runner and
    `process_owner.run_owned`), so Cargo cannot auto-start a server inside a
    job that is terminated as soon as the lane's command finishes.

scripts.common.process_owner.run_finite.decoded_text:
Own a finite command, draining chunks without retaining a full transcript.

    `observe` receives decoded chunks before diagnostic-tail truncation. Full logs
    are deliberately not persisted; callers must reject truncated machine output.
    The deadline covers the primary command. Once it exits, owned descendants
    are stopped before the remaining output is drained, so inherited pipes
    cannot keep an already completed command waiting until its deadline.

scripts.common.process_owner.run_finite.raw_literal:

    The deadline covers the primary command. Once it exits, owned descendants
    are stopped before the remaining output is drained, so inherited pipes
    cannot keep an already completed command waiting until its deadline.
    """

unknown sections and malformed fields remain explicit; complete natural-language interpretation is not claimed
types/defaults/conditions are text, never evaluated; spelling differences need semantic review
effects are bounded syntax candidates; absent sections do not prove undocumented runtime effects
no automatic cross-revision identity mapping, contract admission, test coverage or oracle discharge
function inventory follows the existing collector; nested functions, inherited docs and runtime __doc__ changes are not modeled

contextlib.suppress group semantics follow host Python (recursive since 3.12); jaraco contracts are source-based, not installed-version verification
no injected asynchronous exceptions or resource exhaustion within closed synchronous paths
task child body outcomes are independent candidates, not scheduling, cancellation, join or success evidence

only fresh direct trap contexts and synchronous known decorators; existing trap reuse and arbitrary ExitStack callbacks remain unknown
generator contexts require zero arguments and one expression yield; async cleanup and filesystem/global-state restoration retain conditional contracts only
zero-argument direct helper calls only; no arbitrary parameter, heap or traceback-mutation interpretation
exceptiongroup.catch is not treated as native except*: version-specific handler-error merging is unknown

exception_flow.scope: bounded body-entry-conditional static exception flow; no project code executed

execution_receipt.dependency_policy: bundled worker and host standard library only; project dependencies are not imported or installed
execution_receipt.environment_policy: inherited; Python environment and user site ignored; site startup disabled; UTF-8 forced; launcher overrides removed
limitations: Launcher bytes and path binding checked at endpoints, not an atomic runtime snapshot.
Runtime DLLs, standard-library bytes and non-Python inherited environment are not fully fingerprinted; receipt is not a reusable environment lock.

installed_distribution_evidence.external_contracts: unverified; matching metadata/source bytes do not validate a library model
limitations: Only explicit metadata paths and selected source files are read; absence here never proves a missing dependency.
No site/.pth/egg-link processing, import hooks, namespace resolution, build backends or package execution.
Requires-Dist, extras, wheel tags and Requires-Python are evidence, not evaluated constraints or active graph edges.
Direct URLs are origin claims, not source freshness; editable source needs an explicit source_root and sources.
RECORD can omit hashes/files; only selected SHA-256/size pairs are checked, not complete installation integrity.
Endpoint checks cannot detect change-and-restore or provide an atomic filesystem snapshot; no persistent reuse.
static direct/imported call graph; dynamic dispatch and runtime monkeypatching are unresolved

test roots are test_*.py, *_test.py, legacy test.py, Test-prefixed classes without authored constructors and directly inherited unittest test classes; imported/inherited tests, __test__ overrides and custom runner collection are not resolved
pytest fixture edges include visible authored module/class/ancestor-conftest definitions; imported fixtures, plugins, dynamic requests, scope validity and lifecycle execution remain conditional

pytest marks and parameter rows are declarations, not selected or executed cases; exact case identities must come from named runner evidence and are not preserved across renames by a content fingerprint
boundary coverage uses bounded literal control flow, not observed execution; wrappers, async/generator driving and complex control flow remain unknown
direct await permits a helper-oracle candidate, not proof of scheduling, resumption, cancellation safety or completion
generator-expression bodies require an unmodeled consumer; only the outer iterable is evaluated at creation
arbitrary exception handlers, context-manager suppression, module initialization and mutable closure values are not fully interpreted
native assertions assume non-optimized test execution; compile validation never executes code
closed literal return dictionaries only for field/absence/parameter proofs
object protocols are conditional C3/descriptor candidates; custom hooks, heap state, runtime transformations and library versions remain unverified
Attrs summaries model explicit attr/attrs imports only; generated methods are not authored call edges
Attrs declaration constraints are conditional, not enforced post-construction invariants; package version, callback effects, global validator state and deep heap mutations are unverified

- Structure: ## Overview -> ## Workflow Decision Tree -> ## Step 1 -> ## Step 2...

**2. Task-Based** (best for tool collections)
- Works well when the skill offers different operations/capabilities
- Example: PDF skill with "Quick Start" -> "Merge PDFs" -> "Split PDFs" -> "Extract Text"
- Structure: ## Overview -> ## Quick Start -> ## Task Category 1 -> ## Task Category 2...

**3. Reference/Guidelines** (best for standards or specifications)
- Works well for brand guidelines, coding standards, or requirements
- Example: Brand styling with "Brand Guidelines" -> "Colors" -> "Typography" -> "Features"
- Structure: ## Overview -> ## Guidelines -> ## Specifications -> ## Usage...

**4. Capabilities-Based** (best for integrated systems)
- Works well when the skill provides multiple interrelated features
- Example: Product Management with "Core Capabilities" -> numbered capability list
- Structure: ## Overview -> ## Core Capabilities -> ### 1. Feature -> ### 2. Feature...

Patterns can be mixed and matched as needed. Most skills combine patterns (e.g., start with task-based, add workflow for complex operations).

### scripts/
Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.) that can be run directly to perform specific operations.

**Examples from other skills:**

- DOCX skill: `document.py`, `utilities.py` - Python modules for document processing

**Appropriate for:** Python scripts, shell scripts, or any executable code that performs automation, data processing, or specific operations.

**Note:** Scripts may be executed without loading into context, but can still be read by Codex for patching or environment adjustments.

### references/
Documentation and reference material intended to be loaded into context to inform Codex's process and thinking.

**Examples from other skills:**
- Product management: `communication.md`, `context_building.md` - detailed workflow guides
- BigQuery: API reference documentation and query examples
- Finance: Schema documentation, company policies

**Appropriate for:** In-depth documentation, API references, database schemas, comprehensive guides, or any detailed information that Codex should reference while working.

### assets/
Files not intended to be loaded into context, but rather used within the output Codex produces.

**Examples from other skills:**
- Brand styling: PowerPoint template files (.pptx), logo files
- Frontend builder: HTML/React boilerplate project directories
- Typography: Font files (.ttf, .woff2)

scripts.common.process_owner.run_finite.docstring:
Own a finite command, draining chunks without retaining a full transcript.

`observe` receives decoded chunks before diagnostic-tail truncation. Full logs
are deliberately not persisted; callers must reject truncated machine output.
The deadline covers the primary command. Once it exits, owned descendants
are stopped before the remaining output is drained, so inherited pipes
cannot keep an already completed command waiting until its deadline.

scripts.common.process_owner.run_owned.docstring:
Run once; reap owned descendants before draining terminal output.

Timeout/cancellation exceptions retain captured ``output`` and ``stderr``.
They remain failures even when cleanup successfully closes both pipes.

sdk.python.src.openai_codex.docstring:

Start with :class:`Codex` for synchronous applications or
:class:`AsyncCodex` for async applications. Most programs create a thread and
run a turn::

    from openai_codex import Codex, Sandbox

    with Codex() as codex:
        thread = codex.thread_start(sandbox=Sandbox.workspace_write)
        result = thread.run("Describe this project.")
        print(result.final_response)

sdk.python.src.openai_codex._sandbox.San.docstring:
Preset filesystem access levels for threads and turns.

`read_only` allows file reads without writes. `workspace_write` is the
normal default for projects with a recorded trust decision and allows

Lifecycle operations should hang off the client rather than thread objects.

The importable package version should stay aligned with pyproject metadata.
The wheel should advertise that inline type information is available.
The package root should expose the supported SDK surface, not internals.
The root package should expose the high-level approval mode enum.
The friendly sandbox API should expose only obvious named presets.
The root package should expose the collected turn result wrapper.
